title: Item
description: One catalogued file. Written only by the agent; the web module reads and never writes. The NAS is the source of truth and this document is a mirror of it — if the two disagree, the NAS is right and the next scan corrects the mirror.

id.description: Firestore document id. The content hash, so identical files across sources collapse to one document.

source.description: Which connector this item was catalogued from.

path.description: Connector-native id — for the NAS, the path relative to the share root. This is what an intent's item_id carries.

content_hash.description: The join key for every derived blob. Cheap fingerprint: file size plus a SHA-1 of the first and last 64 KB, so it never reads a whole file over the mount. Thumbnails live at 'thumbs/<hash>.webp'.

thumb.description: Blob key of the 400px WebP thumbnail, once pushed. Derivable from content_hash; stored explicitly so the UI can tell 'not yet generated' from 'generated'.

taken_at.description: Capture time from EXIF where available, falling back to mtime. What the UI sorts by.

latitude.description: From EXIF GPS, where present. Most photos have none — screenshots, edited exports, cameras with GPS off.

duration_seconds.description: Video length, where present. Best-effort within the same head-read budget as the rest of this item's EXIF — a video whose duration atom wasn't in that window (common for large, non-"fast start" files) comes back null, not an error.

focal_length.description: Lens focal length as shot (e.g. "4.2 mm").

focal_length_35mm.description: 35mm-equivalent focal length, for comparing across sensor sizes.

person_ids.description: Ids into the people collection, one per distinct face-cluster detected in this item (photos only). Opaque ids only -- face embeddings (the data that actually makes a face identifiable/matchable) never leave the agent's local catalog; see `faces` for the one thing that does cross, and why that's still safe to publish. Empty unless FACES_LIVE was on when this item was published.

bbox.description: [x1, y1, x2, y2], each a 0-1 fraction of the full original image's own width/height -- not pixel coordinates, and not relative to `thumb` specifically, since that's a differently-sized derivative. Lets the web crop a person's representative thumbnail to their actual face via CSS, without needing a new cropped image asset. null if the image's dimensions weren't known at publish time (rare -- EXIF missing them).

score.description: The face detector's own confidence (insightface's det_score, typically 0-1) that this detection is really a face. A low score is the usual sign of a false positive -- a pattern or texture the model mistook for one -- so the web treats a low-confidence bbox as untrustworthy for cropping rather than zooming into whatever it guessed.

faces.description: One entry per face in `person_ids`, pairing each with just its location in the frame -- a bounding box alone reveals nothing about who someone is (that requires the embedding, which stays local), so this is a deliberate, narrow exception to 'no biometric data leaves the agent,' not a relaxation of it. See CLAUDE.md's face-detection design note.

phash.description: 64-bit perceptual (difference) hash, hex string, photos only. Items whose hash lands close together (small Hamming distance) are visually similar -- a resize, a re-compression, a burst-sequence shot -- and are grouped for review in the web module's Duplicates tab. Never used to auto-archive anything; only a full-content SHA-256 match does that (see dedup.py).

indexed_at.description: When the agent last wrote this document.

state.description: 'trashed' means a delete action moved it to the NAS trash folder. The document stays so the deletion is visible and reversible.
